newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains fed cattle bid $63, passed - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains fed cattle bid $63, passed - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle early Thursday were bid $63.00 per cwt and being passed by owners pricing cattle at $64.00 to $65.00, feedlot sources said.
The bulk of this week's sales were on Tuesday at $63.00 and several pens of those cattle in Kansas were being shipped this morning, sources there said.
Several cattle feeders said a standoff was developing between owners and packers, with owners refusing to sell below $64.00 because they would lose money.
"I guess they think they are current enough to hold onto the cattle another week," a Kansas source said.

Packers reportedly only had enough cattle supplies bought to meet needs into early next week, which has some cattle feeders optimistic that prices could rebound as those packers come back to buy more cattle.
A winter storm in Kansas and Oklahoma Thursday could disrupt transportation, they said.

Local forecasters were calling for up to six inches of snow in western through southeastern Kansas and most of Oklahoma, with coverage also possible in the Texas Panhandle, several sources in those areas said.
